name: אֶפְרַיִם
summary: Joseph's second son by Asenath, born in Egypt, whom Jacob set before Manasseh the firstborn, and the tribe from him, whose host marched under Elishama son of Ammihud (Num 10:22). Joseph gives the reason for the name himself: “God has made me fruitful (הִפְרַנִי) in the land of my affliction” (Gen 41:52), the hiphil of פָּרָה. The ending is that of a dual, as some read it, “doubly fruitful”, though the text gives only the verb. Jacob calls Joseph “a fruitful one” (Gen 49:22), and Hosea plays on the name: Ephraim “is fruitful among his brothers” (Hos 13:15), and Yahweh says to him, “from me is your fruit found” (Hos 14:9).

evidence.note: “The name of the second he called אֶפְרָיִם, for ‘God הִפְרַנִי in the land of my affliction’.”
“The standard of the camp of the sons of אֶפְרַיִם set out by their hosts, and over its host Elishama son of Ammihud.”
Jacob “set Ephraim before Manasseh” in blessing them.
“Joseph is בֵּן פֹּרָת”, a fruitful one: the same verb's participle.
Of Ephraim (Hos 13:12): “though he יַפְרִיא among his brothers”, a play on his name.
“אֶפְרַיִם, what have I to do any more with idols? … From me is your פְּרִי found.”
“Ephraim is struck, their root is dried up, they shall make no פְּרִי”: the name turned against him.

note: BDB a.fh.ae is the name (180 tokens); the database's root for it is אפר, but Gen 41:52 ties it to פרה with a prosthetic א. The key also covers the hill country and forest of Ephraim and the town of 2Sa 13:23 and Jhn 11:54, which are places and are not tagged. The gentilic אֶפְרָתִי (a.fh.ah) is left unclaimed: it names Ephraimites (Jdg 12:5; 1Sa 1:1; 1Ki 11:26) but also Ephrathites of Bethlehem (Rut 1:2; 1Sa 17:12), so tagging it to Ephraim would mislabel two of its five tokens.
